response.justification: While the candidate demonstrates strong software engineering maturity and 16+ years of development experience, they are fundamentally misaligned with this C++ specialist role for industrial automation. Their last significant C++ work ended in 2015 (over 10 years ago), and their entire recent career (2015-present) has focused on web and full-stack development with JavaScript/TypeScript/Node.js. The role explicitly requires current C++ expertise with STL, multi-threaded systems, and industrial automation knowledge; the candidate lacks industrial domain experience, has no background in industrial cybersecurity or IEC 62443 standards, and would require substantial ramp-up time in both C++ proficiency and domain knowledge.
strengths: 16+ years of full-stack development experience demonstrating ability to master multiple languages and architectural patterns across diverse domains
Strong mentoring and knowledge-sharing demonstrated through workshops, code kata sessions, and community speaking engagements at major conferences
Proven expertise in high-performance systems, low-latency optimization, and event-driven architectures including async I/O and concurrent programming concepts
concerns: Critical gap in C++ expertise: last significant C++ development was in 2015 (10+ years ago), with all recent work in JavaScript/TypeScript/Node.js, making readiness for C++ specialist role highly questionable
Complete absence of industrial automation, IoT, or manufacturing domain experience; background is entirely web, GIS, and media-focused with no familiarity with industrial protocols, MQTT, or systems

No demonstrated experience with security-critical development including Secure Development Lifecycle (SDL), IEC 62443 standards, or industrial cybersecurity practices that are core competencies for this role
